title: cadence-aware-throughput-sentinel-and-delayed-cutover-throttle
author: Marta Ruiz
release_notes: Add cadence-aware throughput sentinel: detects periodic cadence-driven throughput dips and gates rollouts with a delayed-cutover throttle to avoid noisy rollback on predictable traffic patterns.
description:
Motivation: We saw a number of false-positive throughput regressions during canaries where downstream traffic cadence (crons / batch windows) produced short-lived throughput dips that triggered aggressive rollback policies. This PR implements a cadence-aware sentinel that (1) models recurring traffic cadence for a target route, (2) applies a delay window before cutover throttles escalate, and (3) exposes configuration knobs for SREs to tune detection sensitivity.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a new sentinel module: cadence_throughput_sentinel (Go) that computes a traffic cadence fingerprint using exponential smoothing over multiple periodicities (1m, 5m, 1h). The fingerprint is used to normalize observed throughput deltas.
- Implements a delayed-cutover throttle controller that defers hard rollback/fallbacks for X windows when the cadence model predicts a transient dip. The controller integrates with existing rollout guards as a pre-check.
- Adds a lightweight probe scheduler change to tag synthetic probes with 'cadence_context' so probes are evaluated against the appropriate baseline.
- Adds telemetry: cadence.match_score, cadence.normalized_throughput_delta, and throttle.defer_reason to tracing and metrics.
- Adds end-to-end tests and a load test harness scenario that simulates hourly batch drains to validate non-triggering of rollbacks.

Design notes and algorithms: The sentinel uses an ensemble of damped-sine detectors and EWMA to capture recurring periodicity without introducing heavy spectral analysis. For each route we maintain: recent throughput time series, last-24h periodicity estimate, and a short-mem EWMA to capture current trend. Normalized delta = (observed - expected_by_cadence) / expected_by_cadence. If normalized delta < threshold AND cadence_match_score > 0.65, the sentinel will mark the event as 'cadence-consistent' and apply the delayed-cutover throttle. The delay window defaults to 3 sample windows (configurable via console or rollout policy).

- services/canary/sentinels/cadence_throughput_sentinel.go (new)
- services/canary/controller/delayed_throttle_controller.go (new)
- services/canary/scheduler/probe_scheduler.go (tagging probes)
- observability/metrics/metrics_registry.go (new metrics)
- tests/e2e/canary_cadence_scenarios_test.go (load + unit test harness)
- docs/runbooks/canary-cadence.md (operator guidance)

- dashboards/cadence-sentinel.json (grafana panel)
- go.mod / go.sum (deps)

Commits (high level):
- 7a2c4b2: initial cadence sentinel prototype and unit tests
- 9b3d1f7: delayed throttle controller and integration with rollout-manager
- d1f6e2a: add metrics + tracing tags and dashboard JSON
- e2a8b4c: e2e load test that simulates hourly batch drain pattern
- f4b9c5d: docs + runbook + example traffic profile

Test plan:
- Unit tests cover cadence model edge cases (cold start, missing data, noisy inputs).
- E2E harness runs two scenarios: steady load + hourly drain burst; and irregular spikes. Both scenarios are run in CI and locally using the perf-canary harness. CI includes a synthetic traffic replay (small dataset) to validate matching/normalization heuristics.
- Performance: sentinel adds ~0.5ms median CPU time per canary evaluation (benchmarked on small instance). Memory overhead is bounded (per-route 128-512KB states).

Observability and runbook:
- New grafana panels for cadence.match_score and normalized deltas.
- Runbook doc describes how to interpret cadence.match_score, tuning thresholds, and emergency disablement of the sentinel if it masks real regressions.

Reviewer notes & discussion (excerpt):
- Omar: "How do we avoid masking slow regressions that coincide with cadence?"
  Marta: "We added a cross-check that if absolute token-latency change exceeds a hard SLO delta (configurable, default 20%) we bypass delay and escalate immediately. This is documented in code comments and tests."
- Leah: "Can we expose per-customer opt-out?"
  Marta: "Added opt-out flag at rollout policy level; also added feature flag and console toggle for tenant-scoped behaviour."
- Diego: "Load testing looks good but add more noisy traffic scenarios."
  Marta: "Added an irregular-spike scenario and increased sample size in e2e harness."

CI summary: all unit tests and e2e harness passed in CI. Linting required one minor import style fix (auto-fixed). Benchmarks included in artifacts; synthetic traffic replay ran on github Actions runner in ~18m.

Merge & rollout plan:
- Merged via squash. Feature gated behind 'cadence-sentinel' feature flag.
- Gradual rollout to canary traffic first (5% routes) for 48 hours, monitor cadence.match_score > 0.6 and any suppressed rollbacks. If no missed regressions and metrics stable, increase to 25% then 100% over a week.

Backout plan: feature flag + immediate disable in rollout-manager UI; run a quick regression canary on baseline models to verify no masked regressions.

Why different from previous work: Existing detectors focus on raw percentiles and entropy; this PR focuses on modeling predictable recurring traffic cadence (cron/batch windows) and provides a conservative delayed throttle to reduce noisy rollback churn without sacrificing safety (hard latency cross-check bypass).

Notes for docs/SDK: Operator docs and an example quickstart were added to docs/runbooks. The TypeScript console uses the new metrics endpoints to render cadence panels (small console patch included in follow-up PR).

Follow-ups:
- Add optional spectral-analysis mode (disabled by default) for routes with strong multi-frequency patterns.
- Add tenant-scoped configuration via private installer for regulated customers.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] E2E harness and load profile
- [x] Observability dashboards
- [x] Runbook and release notes
- [x] Feature flag gating

Merge outcome: Squash merged to main on 2026-02-18 after approvals from Omar and Leah.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the cadence model lightweight to reduce CPU and memory footprint; heavyweight spectral transforms were deferred to follow-ups behind an opt-in flag. The runbook stresses conservative thresholds to avoid masking genuine regressions.
